title: Catholics disagree
hookLine: the Church holds deep disagreements within one communion
tomorrow: Year four close: the house of many rooms

lines: THE NEIGHBOR IN THE SAME PEW.
cards: Sunday lunch after Mass. Grandpa misses the Latin. His granddaughter loves the guitar Mass.
An uncle reads one Catholic newspaper, an aunt reads another, and they have opinions about each other's. Somebody says the word bishop and the table goes quiet.

All of them went to the same Mass that morning, all received communion, and all will be back next week. After days of neighbors of other faiths and none, today's neighbor sits across the table, in the same pew.

teach.h: PAUL WITHSTOOD PETER TO HIS FACE.
teach.b: Start with the apostles, because they argued too. You met this clash on day six hundred seventy-five, with the two pillars.
In Galatians, Paul describes facing Peter at Antioch over eating with Gentile believers, and he doesn't soften it. In the Douay-Rheims: "I withstood him to the face."
Two apostles, one Church, a public disagreement, and the New Testament keeps it on the record.
The Catechism says that from the beginning the one Church has been marked by great diversity, because God gives many different gifts and the people receiving them differ too.

teach.h: ONE FAITH, ONE WORSHIP, ONE BOND OF LOVE.
teach.b: What holds it together: one faith professed, common worship and sacraments, and the succession of bishops from the apostles. Above all, it says, is charity, the bond of perfection. So the Church draws a line.

Some things belong to the faith itself, and there it asks for unity. Other questions are left open: how to apply teaching to a hard case, which style of prayer helps, which school of theology makes the most sense.
Dominican and Jesuit theologians once argued so hard about how grace works that a pope finally let both schools keep teaching, and told them to stop calling each other heretics.

An old Latin saying, which Pope John XXIII quoted, gives the shape: in necessary things unity, in doubtful things liberty, in all things charity. That's one communion up close. Not everyone thinking alike.

how: Catholics share one profession of faith and the same sacraments while holding different views on many open questions, from theology to liturgy to politics. Parishes include people who disagree, and the Church allows different schools of theology and spirituality within its communion.

o: holding real differences inside one faith and one altar
arguments the Church forbids its members ever to have
a sign the Church has quietly split into two churches

games.q: unity, not sameness — tap the pairs.
p: the bond above all the others

s: the apostles always agreed with each other
in Galatians, Paul says he withstood Peter to his face at Antioch.
the Catechism says diversity has marked the Church from the beginning
it traces it to the variety of God's gifts and of the people who receive them.
every question is settled, so Catholics may not hold different views

games.q: Dominican and Jesuit theologians are accusing each other of heresy over how grace works. you're the pope. what do you do?
o: declare one side right and silence the other.
let both schools keep teaching, and tell them to stop calling each other heretics.
games.why: the pope let both schools keep teaching and forbade them to call each other heretics: a disagreement held inside one communion.

practice: Choose one person you disagree with, about church, or politics, or how to raise children, someone you'll actually see this week, and find one thing you genuinely share: a person you both love, a meal you've eaten together, a Mass you've both been to.
Hold that, then shape one sentence that names your view without belittling theirs. If you pray, you can ask for patience for you both.

wordCard.voice: Catholics disagree. From the apostles on, the Church has held real disagreements inside one faith, one worship and one bond of charity. Today's word.

orig.s: in necessariis unitas, in dubiis libertas, in omnibus caritas
orig.note: Latin: in necessary things unity, in doubtful things liberty, in all things charity; a saying Pope John XXIII quoted.

carryVoice: Your line: unity, not sameness. Above every disagreement, charity, the bond of perfection. Until tomorrow.
